topic: lie detection - overexplaining as a tell
title: The Real Reason Liars Get Caught (Hint: It's Not Nerves)
description: AI-narrated commentary on the psychology of lie detection: why liars often get caught by adding too much unprompted detail, not by looking nervous. An interesting behavioral pattern, not investigative or legal advice. #psychology #shorts

hook_candidates.text: Forget eye contact, that's not how liars actually get caught.
Most liars aren't caught by nervousness, they're caught by adding one detail nobody asked for.
Why do liars almost always over-explain the one detail that matters least?

beats.text: Most liars don't get caught by acting nervous, they get caught by adding one detail nobody asked for.
Psychologists call it unprompted elaboration, when someone volunteers specifics no one requested, it's often their brain trying too hard to sound believable.
Truthful memories are messy, people forget small things and correct themselves mid-sentence.
Fabricated stories are usually smoother, because they were rehearsed instead of remembered.
Real investigators don't watch for shifty eyes, they watch for stories that are a little too clean.
Next time someone's explanation sounds suspiciously polished, ask one follow-up question you didn't plan, and tell me in the comments if it's ever worked for you.
